owner_action: Charge to 100 percent once a week. The car runs a maintenance routine that only works at a full charge.
clause_verbatim: This vehicle has an automatic maintenance function that works when the high voltage battery is fully charged. To maintain the high voltage battery performance, fully charge the battery once a week. However, if the vehicle is not used for an extended period of time, refrain from storing the high voltage battery fully charged to prevent deterioration. [Printed p79 and repeated p82, in a NOTICE box under the heading 'High voltage battery (lithium-ion battery)'.]

owner_action: Do not leave it standing at 100 percent for a long spell. The weekly full charge is for a car in use, not a car being stored.
clause_verbatim: This vehicle has an automatic maintenance function that works when the high voltage battery is fully charged. To maintain the high voltage battery performance, fully charge the battery once a week. However, if the vehicle is not used for an extended period of time, refrain from storing the high voltage battery fully charged to prevent deterioration. [Printed p79 and repeated p82, in a NOTICE box under the heading 'High voltage battery (lithium-ion battery)'.]

owner_action: If the car is laid up, charge it at least once a month, and not to full.
clause_verbatim: If the vehicle is not used for an extended period of time, charge the high voltage battery at least once a month to prevent it from becoming extremely undercharged. Do not fully charge the high voltage battery to prevent deterioration and charge it before the low high voltage battery warning light lights. [Printed p79, under the heading 'If the vehicle is not used for an extended period of time'.]

owner_action: Do not leave the cable connected or the flap open when you are not charging. It drains the 12 volt battery.
clause_verbatim: To prevent the 12-volt battery from losing power, do not leave the charging cover open or the charging cable connected to the vehicle. [Printed p79, chapter 2 Electric vehicle system.]

owner_action: If the car will stand unused, pull the plug out of the wall socket.
clause_verbatim: If the vehicle will be unused for a long period of time, pull the plug out of the power outlet. [Printed p106, step 4 of the procedure 'When disconnecting the AC charging connector'.]

owner_action: Avoid frequent DC charging, and do not park at 100 percent in the sun. Both are named as causes of lost capacity.
clause_verbatim: To prevent a drop off in battery capacity, keep the following points in mind. Avoid parking the vehicle in a hot, sunny location when it is fully charged. No frequent acceleration and deceleration when driving. Avoid driving near the maximum speed. Use charging schedule to fully charge the battery before you start driving. Avoid frequent DC charging. [Printed p101, under the heading 'Decreased high voltage battery capacity'.]

owner_action: Avoid frequent DC charging. The maker names it as a cause of lost capacity.
clause_verbatim: To prevent a decrease in the high voltage battery capacity, you are recommended to avoid frequent DC charging. [Printed p109, in the WARNING list headed 'While DC charging'.]

owner_action: Use a cable Toyota specifies, or one from the maker of the charging equipment.
clause_verbatim: Connect the charging cable specified by Toyota or the manufacturer of the equipment for charging to the charging inlet. [Printed p11, under the sub-heading 'Charging inlet'.]

owner_action: The car puts a message on the dashboard if you keep charging without ever filling it. You can see this one.
clause_verbatim: CHARGE 100% FOR MORE EFFICIENT HV BATTERY USAGE. The vehicle is being used repeatedly without fully charging the high voltage battery. Fully charge the battery. To maintain the high voltage battery performance, it is recommended to fully charge the battery once a week. [Printed p176, in the table of meter display messages. This is a message the owner can read on the dashboard.]

clause_verbatim: If the vehicle is not used for an extended period of time, charge the traction battery at least once a month to prevent it from becoming extremely undercharged. Do not fully charge the traction battery to prevent deterioration and charge it before the low traction battery warning light lights. [Printed p85, under the heading 'If the vehicle is not used for an extended period of time'.]

owner_action: Do not store it where it gets very hot or very cold. In summer, park in shade.
clause_verbatim: Do not store the vehicle in areas with extremely high or low outside temperatures. In midsummer, you can keep the lithium-ion battery longer by parking in the shade rather than in the blazing sun. [Printed p88, NOTICE box.]

owner_action: Avoid frequent DC charging, and do not park at 100 percent in the sun. Both are named as causes of lost capacity.
clause_verbatim: To prevent a drop off in battery capacity, keep the following points in mind. Avoid parking the vehicle in a hot, sunny location when it is fully charged. No frequent acceleration and deceleration when driving. Avoid driving at or around the maximum speed. Use timer charging to fully charge the battery before you start driving. Avoid frequent DC charging. [Printed p107, under the heading 'Decreased traction battery capacity'.]

owner_action: Avoid frequent DC charging. The maker names it as a cause of lost capacity.
clause_verbatim: To prevent a decrease in the traction battery capacity, you are recommended to avoid frequent DC charging. [Printed p114, in the WARNING list headed 'While DC charging'.]

owner_action: If the cable will go unused for a long spell, pull the plug out of the wall socket and store the cable dry.
clause_verbatim: Pull the power plug out of the power outlet. Dust can accumulate on the power plug or outlet and cause overheating or fire. Store the AC charging cable in a dry place. [Printed p424, NOTICE box under the heading 'If the AC charging cable will be unused for a long period of time'.]

owner_action: A genuine cable is not enough on its own. It has to be the cable for your model and year.
clause_verbatim: Even if the charging cable is a Maruti Suzuki genuine AC charging cable, it may not be possible to use it if it is designed for another model or a different year model. [Printed p94, under the heading 'AC charging cable'.]

owner_action: The car puts a message on the dashboard if you keep charging without ever filling it. You can see this one.
clause_verbatim: CHARGE 100% FOR MORE EFFICIENT HV BATTERY USAGE. The vehicle is being used repeatedly without fully charging the traction battery. Fully charge the battery. To maintain the traction battery performance, it is recommended to fully charge the battery once a week. [Printed p179, in the table of meter display messages. This is a message the owner can read on the dashboard.]

owner_action: After every four DC fast charges, do one AC charge to 100 percent.
clause_verbatim: Allow AC charging up to 100% State of Charging ("SOC") once in every 4 fast charge (DC) cycles. [Printed p23, under "Care instruction while leaving the Vehicle idle for long duration - For preventing damage to the Battery:". Identical in the BE 6, BE 6 FE and XEV 9e guides.]

owner_action: After four DC fast charges, do one AC charge to 100 percent.
clause_verbatim: Allow AC charging up to 100 % State of Charging ("SOC") once after 4 fast charge (DC) cycles. [Printed p23. The XEV 9S guide says "once after 4" where the other three say "once in every 4".]

owner_action: Keep DC fast charging to a minimum.
clause_verbatim: The use of fast charging should be minimized to help prolong life of the Battery. [Printed p23, same list. Identical in all four guides.]

owner_action: If the car stops because the battery ran flat, plug it in within 24 hours or the battery warranty is void.
clause_verbatim: Vehicle stopped due to over discharge of Battery and is not plugged for charge within 24 hours from time of stoppage. [Printed p22, in the list headed "In addition to the EXCLUSIONS TO WARRANTY listed above, the Battery warranty will be null and void if:". Identical in all four guides.]

owner_action: The care instructions on the next page are not advice. Not following them forfeits the battery warranty.
clause_verbatim: Vehicle missing any of Battery service requirements as specified or not adhering to the conditions set out above, or not adhering to conditions mentioned in the Vehicle Manual, will forfeit warranty on Battery. [Printed p22, closing the null-and-void list. This is what turns the page 23 care instructions into warranty conditions.]

owner_action: Do not run it below 5 percent often.
clause_verbatim: Do not drain the Battery to less than 5% state of charge frequently, as deep discharges can harm to the Battery health. [Printed p23. Grammatical error is the maker's.]

owner_action: If it sits idle, charge to 30 to 40 percent at least once every two months.
clause_verbatim: While the vehicle is idle, ensure to charge the vehicle to at least 30% to 40% SOC at least once in two months, to prevent deep discharge. [Printed p23.]

owner_action: Never leave it idle more than six months.
clause_verbatim: Never leave the vehicle idle for more than 6 months at a time. [Printed p23.]

owner_action: Do not charge or park in extreme heat or cold.
clause_verbatim: Avoid vehicle charging and parking in extreme ambient temperatures (hot or cold). [Printed p23.]

owner_action: Do not charge if the socket or port is damaged or wet.
clause_verbatim: Do not charge the vehicle, if the power socket/charge port is damaged or exposed to rain or water. [Printed p23.]

owner_action: Do a slow AC charge to 100 percent every 15 days, or after every four DC charges, whichever comes first.
clause_verbatim: Slow AC charging till 100% SoC is recommended at least once a 15 Days or after every 4 fast DC/opportunity charging cycles whichever is earlier, for SoC calibration & cell balancing. [Printed p3-16, under "Charging tips". Spacing and grammar are the maker's.]

owner_action: Charging past 90 percent is when the pack balances its cells and re-references the gauge, which is why MG asks you to finish at 100 percent.
clause_verbatim: Cell balancing and equalization, as well as state of charge (SoC) calibration, occur during charging, particularly when the SoC is above 90%. This results in longer charging times when exceeding 90%. It is recommended to allow the vehicle to charge to 100% SoC before ending the charging session. [Printed p3-17, under "Cell Balancing & equalization".]

owner_action: Charge to 100 percent every time you charge.
clause_verbatim: It is recommended to charge the vehicle to 100%, whenever vehicle is being charged. [Printed p3-16, under "Charging tips".]

owner_action: On a new car, do a full 100 percent charge before it first drops below 30 percent.
clause_verbatim: After you receive the vehicle, make sure to fully charge the HV battery to 100% before it drops below 30% to keep it in good condition. [Printed p1-2.]

owner_action: Charge to full at least once every two weeks in normal use.
clause_verbatim: It is recommended to fully charge the battery at least once every two weeks when using the vehicle regularly for maintenance. [Printed p1-3, under "Battery maintenance".]

owner_action: Store above 50 percent. Once a month, charge it fully on AC then run it down to 40 to 60 percent before parking again. MG says over-discharge damage may not be covered.
clause_verbatim: Before storing the vehicle for an extended period (over one month), ensure the battery is charged to more than 50%. After prolonged parking, perform charging maintenance at least once a month. This involves fully charging the vehicle using AC slow charging, then discharging it to between 40% and 60% before parking again. Failure to maintain the battery as recommended could lead to vehicle issues caused by over-discharge, which may not be covered under warranty. [Printed p1-4, in a WARNING box.]

owner_action: Do not drive below 10 percent.
clause_verbatim: Avoid driving vehicle below 10% SOC. [Printed p3-16, under "Charging tips".]

owner_action: Do not charge in a thunderstorm or outdoors in the rain.
clause_verbatim: Do not charge the vehicle in thunder and lightning conditions, and do not charge in the open air on rainy days. Otherwise, it may damage the charging equipment, or cause lightning strike and electric shock. [Printed p3-16, in a DANGER box.]

owner_action: The socket must be wired correctly and properly earthed. Adapters, reels and power strips are prohibited.
clause_verbatim: The wiring of the socket should be correct (live wire, neutral wire and earth wire), and the earth wire should be reliably earthed. Transfers using adapters, reels, power strips, etc. are prohibited. [Printed p3-3.]

owner_action: Charge to 80 percent for daily use and keep DC fast charging to a minimum.
clause_verbatim: If the HV battery is only charged to 80%, and you minimise the number of DC fast charging, you can keep the HV battery performance in optimal condition. [Printed p7-4 of the Carens Clavis EV manual and the equivalent page of the EV9 manual. The Kia Syros EV manual was checked for this sentence and does not carry it.]

owner_action: Use AC charging as the normal way to charge.
clause_verbatim: AC (L2-Normal) charging is recommended to keep the high voltage battery in optimal condition. [Printed p7-4.]

owner_action: If it is laid up, charge it every three months, and charge it full before you leave it.
clause_verbatim: If the vehicle will not be in use for an extended period of time, charge the high voltage battery once every three months to prevent it from discharging. Also, if the charge amount is not enough, immediately charge to full before leaving the vehicle. [Printed p7-4.]

owner_action: Do not let the gauge sit on empty. Kia says the pack may need replacing.
clause_verbatim: Make sure that the HV battery charge gauge does not reach E (Empty). If the vehicle is kept at E (Empty) for a long period, it may damage the high voltage battery and the high voltage battery may have to be replaced, depending on the level of degradation. [Printed p7-5, in a CAUTION box.]

owner_action: Use a designated charger. Kia says other chargers seriously affect durability.
clause_verbatim: Make sure to use a designated charger when charging the HV battery. Using different types of chargers may have a serious impact on vehicle durability. [Printed p7-5, in a CAUTION box.]

owner_action: Use only a Kia certified cable. No extension reels.
clause_verbatim: Only use the charging cable (if equipped) certified by Kia. Using a separate extension cable, such as a reel or an uncertified cable, may cause abnormalities in electrical outlets, leading to fire or explosion. [Printed p7-32, under "Precautions for charging electric vehicle".]

owner_action: Keep DC charging to a minimum.
clause_verbatim: Use of DC charge should be minimized in order to help prolong high voltage battery life. [Printed p2-20 of the IONIQ 5 manual and p H13 of the Kona Electric manual. Identical sentence in both.]

owner_action: Prefer AC. If you drop below 20 percent, charge to 100 percent, at least monthly.
clause_verbatim: AC charge is recommended to keep the high voltage battery in optimal condition. If the high voltage battery charge amount is below 20%, you can keep the high voltage battery performance in optimal condition if you charge the high voltage battery to 100%. (Once a month or more is recommended.) [Printed p2-5 of the IONIQ 5 manual.]

owner_action: If it is laid up, charge it at least every three months.
clause_verbatim: If you do not use the vehicle for a long time, charge the vehicle at least once every 3 months to prevent the battery from fully discharging. [Printed p1-10. This edition replaces the below-20-percent wording of the earlier IONIQ 5 manual.]

owner_action: Use only a specified EV charger.
clause_verbatim: Use specified electric vehicle charger only. Failure to do so may damage the charger, charging cable, or vehicle. Also, it may lead to safety hazards, such as fire, explosion, etc. [Printed p1-13, in a WARNING box.]

owner_action: Charging to 100 percent often, above all when you do not drive straight after, accelerates ageing. So does frequent DC.
clause_verbatim: THE FOLLOWING FACTORS COULD ACCELERATE THE AGEING OF THE HIGH-VOLTAGE BATTERY: frequently fully charging (charge level 100%) the high-voltage battery, especially when this process is not directly followed by a journey; frequent rapid charging with direct current (mode 4); leaving the vehicle idle for lengthy periods at high ambient temperatures. [Printed p287 of the EQA manual, under a boxed note. Capitalisation is the maker's.]

owner_action: Park it at 30 to 50 percent for a long spell, and do not leave it plugged in.
clause_verbatim: In the case of longer idle periods: Park the vehicle with the high-voltage battery at a state of charge between 30 % and 50 %. Do not permanently connect the high-voltage battery to power supply equipment. Avoid high outside temperatures as far as possible. [Printed p288 of the EQA manual and p355 of the EQS SUV manual, under "RECOMMENDATIONS WHEN HANDLING THE HIGH-VOLTAGE BATTERY".]

owner_action: Once every six months, park it overnight below 20 percent when it is warmer than 10 degrees.
clause_verbatim: If the outside temperature is above 10 °C, park the vehicle overnight with a state of charge below 20 % every six months. [Printed p288 of the EQA manual and p355 of the EQS SUV manual.]

owner_action: Check the charge level every six weeks.
clause_verbatim: Check the high-voltage battery's state of charge every six weeks. [Printed p288 of the EQA manual.]

model_scope: 450X, 450S, 450 Apex, Rizta S, Rizta Z, Konarc S
owner_action: Charge it at least once every 100 days even in Shutdown Mode, or the pack can be permanently damaged.
clause_verbatim: Charge your scooter every 100 days. It's a must, even if the scooter is in Shutdown Mode. This prevents permanent damage to the battery pack. [Printed p38, in a CAUTION box under "Scooter shutdown".]

model_scope: 450X, 450S, 450 Apex, Rizta S, Rizta Z, Konarc S
owner_action: Put it in Shutdown Mode if it will stand more than five days.
clause_verbatim: If you are not using your scooter for more than 5 days, leave it in Shutdown Mode to prevent battery drain. [Printed p40, under "THINGS TO KEEP IN MIND WHEN NOT IN USE".]

model_scope: 450X, 450S, 450 Apex, Rizta S, Rizta Z, Konarc S
owner_action: Use the charger Ather supplied. The warranty policy words it as the Ather charger specifically, not an approved equivalent.
clause_verbatim: Always use the original charger provided by Ather to charge your vehicle. Avoid using 3rd party chargers. [Printed p40, under "EXTEND YOUR BATTERY LIFE". Fuller than the warranty policy wording, which does not mention third party chargers.]

owner_action: Charge to 80 percent before a long lay-up and check monthly that it stays above 30 percent.
clause_verbatim: If the vehicle is not going to be used for an extended period of time (long storage), please charge vehicle to 80%. Monthly check to ensure that the High Voltage Battery SOC is always above 30%. [Battery & Charging, Battery Information, under the heading 'Battery Care'.]

owner_action: Do not store it above 35 degrees or below zero. VinFast says this may cause permanent degradation.
clause_verbatim: During storage, the vehicle should not be exposed to ambient temperatures exceeding 35°C or falling below 0°C for extended periods. If extreme temperatures are anticipated, it is recommended to store the vehicle in a climate-controlled garage. Not adhering to these guidelines may result in permanent degradation of the High Voltage Battery's performance. [Battery & Charging, Battery Information, under the heading 'Temperature Limits'.]

owner_action: Keep super fast charging to a minimum.
clause_verbatim: The use of Super Fast Charge Stations should be minimized to ensure the optimal lifetime performance of the battery. [Battery & Charging, Charging Instructions, in a NOTE box.]

owner_action: Never let it go flat.
clause_verbatim: Although the High Voltage battery is maintenance free, it is important to always be aware of the battery state of charge and never allow the battery to fully discharge. [Battery & Charging, Battery Information, under the heading 'Battery Care'.]

owner_action: Set a target below 100 percent for everyday charging. Save 100 percent for a trip you are about to take.
clause_verbatim: The traction battery can sustain damage if the car's battery level is kept very high for a long period of time. For regular charging, battery wear can be reduced by selecting a target battery level lower than 100%. Only charge to 100% if the full range is needed for your next trip. [Under the heading 'High state of charge', in an Important box.]

owner_action: Use AC every day. Volvo says DC causes more wear.
clause_verbatim: AC charging is the recommended charging mode for everyday charging. This helps maintain the condition of the battery over time. DC charging causes more wear. [Under the heading 'Charging habits'.]

owner_action: Park it at 40 to 60 percent over a month, and at 50 percent plugged in over three months.
clause_verbatim: When leaving your car parked for longer than one month, the recommended battery level is 40-60%. Use or charge the car to reach the recommended level. If you are leaving the car parked for longer than three months, it's recommended to keep it plugged in but set a battery charging limit of 50%. This is for better battery health. [Under the heading 'Long-term parking'.]

owner_action: Below 20 percent when parked, plug it in as soon as you can. At zero the damage can be severe.
clause_verbatim: The traction battery can sustain severe damage if it is not charged after the battery level reaches 0%. The car draws a small amount of power when parked. Therefore, leaving the car with a low battery level without charging can lead to a flat battery and battery damage. If the battery level is below 20% when parked, it is recommended that the car is connected for charging as soon as possible. [Under the heading 'Low battery level and flat battery', in an Important box.]

owner_action: Do not leave it parked over 24 hours where it could reach 55 degrees.
clause_verbatim: Avoid exposing the car to extreme temperatures. Avoid leaving the car parked for longer than 24 hours if the temperature is at risk of reaching 55 °C (131 °F). [Under the heading 'Parking in hot weather', in an Important box.]

owner_action: Do not let it sit below 10 percent. Hyundai says the pack may need replacing.
clause_verbatim: Keep the gauge of the high voltage battery from going below than 10 %. Storing the vehicle whilst the battery level is low for a long time may damage the battery or reduce the battery's capacity, potentially causing the need for a battery replacement. [Printed p1-8, in a CAUTION box under "Precautions when using the high voltage battery".]

owner_action: Prefer AC. When you drop to 20 percent or lower, charge to full, at least monthly.
clause_verbatim: To keep the battery in optimal condition, use AC charging. Fully charging the battery when it is 20 % or lower helps to keep the battery in optimal condition. Charging once a month or more is recommended. [Printed p1-8.]

owner_action: Use AC unless you actually need DC. Hyundai says performance and life may deteriorate if DC is used constantly.
clause_verbatim: Battery performance and life may deteriorate if the DC charger is used constantly. Use of DC charging should be minimised in order to help prolong high voltage battery life. Use AC charging unless DC charging is necessary. [Printed p1-15 and repeated p1-25, in CAUTION boxes. The third sentence is the strongest Hyundai India wording and does not appear in the IONIQ 5 or Kona manuals.]

owner_action: If it is laid up, charge it at least every three months.
clause_verbatim: If you do not use the vehicle for a long time, charge the vehicle at least once every 3 months to prevent the battery from fully discharging. When the battery level has lower power, immediately charge the vehicle. [Printed p1-8.]

owner_action: Do not store it somewhere very hot or very cold.
clause_verbatim: Storing the vehicle in temperatures that are too hot or cold may degrade the battery performance. [Printed p1-8.]

owner_action: Use only a specified EV charger.
clause_verbatim: Use specified electric vehicle charger only. Failure to do so may damage the charger, charging cable, or vehicle. Also, it may lead to safety hazards, such as fire, explosion, etc. [Printed p1-11, in a WARNING box.]

owner_action: Hyundai says repeated use of the car as a power source may shorten pack life.
clause_verbatim: Using the V2L function may reduce the driving distance due to the use of the high voltage battery energy, and repeated use of the V2L function may cause a decrease in the life of the high voltage battery. [Printed p1-8.]

owner_action: Use of an improper battery charger is listed as not covered. This is an exclusion, not advice.
clause_verbatim: Use of improper battery charger, fluids or lubricants. [Printed pdf p72, under '3. What is not covered'. Word for word the same clause JSW MG prints for the ZS EV, Comet EV and Windsor EV.]

owner_action: Keep it above 80 percent in long storage. Vida recommends checking weekly and not leaving it unmonitored beyond 100 days, and says failure to comply voids the warranty.
clause_verbatim: Please keep your vehicle SOC > 80% when you intend to keep stored for long periods of time without using, but we recommend you to keep on checking the SOC levels on a weekly basis and not leave the vehicle unmonitored for more than 100 days at a continuous stretch. [Section 11.a General with Long Storage Guidelines, in a CAUTION box.]

owner_action: Vida attaches the warranty to the storage instructions directly.
clause_verbatim: Failure to comply with above instructions will likely cause permanent damage the battery and void the warranty. [Section 11.a, closing the CAUTION box that contains the above 80 percent storage instruction. Grammatical error is the maker's.]

owner_action: Hibernate after five days standing, then recharge.
clause_verbatim: We recommend 5 Day Hibernation for Lithium-Ion Batteries for optimum performance. Post that recharge your Li-Ion Battery. [Section 11.a.]

owner_action: The pack is built to stop working after eight years from first charge and/or 14,000 Ah of accumulated charging. Hero does not say which of the two applies.
clause_verbatim: Battery electric output auto-stopping function | The battery is equipped with a function to prevent further use in case of excessive depletion. When eight years have passed post initial battery charging (at OEM end) and/or the accumulated charging amount reaches 14000 Ah, the traction battery will no longer be usable. [Section 11.b Warning about Scrapping Traction batteries.]

owner_action: Charge to at least 30 percent once every 15 days.
clause_verbatim: Do not leave your vehicle without charging for a long period of time (Vehicles should be charged to 30% SOC atleast once in 15 days). [Printed p14, in the Warning list under SAFE RIDING TIPS.]

owner_action: Charge to at least 50 percent once every 15 days.
clause_verbatim: Do not leave your vehicle without charging for a long period of time (Vehicles should be charged to 50% SOC atleast once in 15 days). [Printed p41. The TVS X figure is 50 percent where the Orbiter manual says 30 percent.]

owner_action: Do not let the battery go above 60 degrees.
clause_verbatim: Do not expose battery to temperature above 60°C. [Printed p14, in a Caution box.]

owner_action: Any electrical work for charging must be done by an authorised electrician.
clause_verbatim: Any electrical work should be performed by authorized electrician only. Failure to do so might result in sever injury or risk to life. [Printed p45 of the Orbiter manual, in a Caution box under CHARGING THE VEHICLE. 'sever' is the maker's spelling. The TVS X manual prints the same sentence with 'severe'.]

owner_action: Any electrical work for charging must be done by an authorised electrician.
clause_verbatim: Any electrical work should be performed by authorized electrician only. Failure to do so might result in severe injury or risk to life. [Printed p42 of the TVS X manual, in a Caution box. The Orbiter manual prints the same sentence but spells it 'sever'.]

owner_action: Earth the wiring, use a 16A socket with an MCB, and fit a surge protector or voltage regulator.
clause_verbatim: Good to do for charging the vehicle at your home: 1. Ensure that domestic wiring is properly grounded. 2. Ensure that socket is having earth connection. 3. Use 16A socket with MCB for charging (Charger will work in 5A socket also). 4. Install surge protector / voltage regulator. [Printed p46.]

owner_action: Supply must be 220 to 240V, single phase, properly earthed. No extension boxes.
clause_verbatim: Input AC voltage should be within the range of 220 to 240V. Need to ensure proper earth connection in the AC domestic power socket. Plug the charger in Single phase AC domestic socket only. Do not use extension box to charge the vehicle for safety purpose. [Printed p43, in a Warning box.]

owner_action: Charge to 100 percent at least once every 60 days, even in sleep mode, or the warranty can be void.
clause_verbatim: To maintain good battery health, please charge your vehicle up to 100% once in 60 days even if it has been kept in sleep mode. Failing to do so may result in voiding your warranty. [Printed p77 of the Gen 3 manual, in a CAUTION box. The Gen 1 and Gen 2 manuals carry the same sentence with 90 days in place of 60.]

owner_action: Charge to 100 percent at least once every 90 days, even in hibernation, or the warranty can be void. The Gen 3 manual shortened this to 60 days.
clause_verbatim: To maintain good battery health, please charge your vehicle up to 100% once in 90 days even if it has been kept in hibernation mode. Failing to do so may result in voiding your warranty. [Printed p26 of the Gen 1 manual, in a CAUTION box. Superseded by the 60 day wording in the Gen 3 manual.]

owner_action: Storing it with too little charge is not covered if the pack degrades.
clause_verbatim: If the vehicle is stored with insufficient charge for a long period of time, it may degrade the battery and the battery may have to be replaced based on the level of degradation. In such cases, warranty shall not be covered. [Printed p23 of the Gen 3 manual, in a NOTICE box. The Gen 1 manual carries the same sentence without the final clause about warranty.]

owner_action: Storing it with too little charge can degrade the pack. The Gen 1 manual stops there and attaches no warranty consequence.
clause_verbatim: If the vehicle is stored with insufficient charge for a long period of time, it may degrade the battery and the battery may have to be replaced based on the level of degradation. In such cases, warranty shall not be covered. [Printed p23 of the Gen 3 manual, in a NOTICE box. The Gen 1 manual carries the same sentence without the final clause about warranty.]

owner_action: Use a voltage protector and circuit breakers. River says out-of-bound surges or grid faults can destroy the charger.
clause_verbatim: It is recommended to use an AC supply provided through a voltage protector (such as: LINK or equivalent) and circuit breakers (such as: LINK or equivalent). Any out-of-bound surges or grid faults may result in irreparable damages to the charger. [Printed p85 of the Gen 3 manual. Absent from the Gen 1 manual.]

owner_action: Before you charge, measure neutral to earth with a multimeter. River says it must read under 3V.
clause_verbatim: Ensure that you are getting less than 3V, using a multimeter across the Neutral and Earth. [Printed p85 of the Gen 3 manual, under Setting up your environment. The Gen 1 manual carries the same check.]

owner_action: Have an electrician do the charging point install and the earth checks.
clause_verbatim: Do not attempt to do the above by yourself. Contract an electrician to install the same and provide the above guidelines. [Printed p30 of the Gen 1 manual, in a DANGER box following the earthing and voltage checks.]

owner_action: The charging guidance in this manual is binding. Not following it can void the warranty.
clause_verbatim: Battery Maintenance: To maintain the battery's longevity and performance, adhere strictly to the charging and maintenance guidelines provided. Failure to follow these guidelines may result in reduced battery life and can void the warranty. [Printed p17, under Battery Maintenance. This is what makes the charging sections of this manual warranty-binding rather than advisory.]

owner_action: Set the app charge limit to 90 percent. Ultraviolette's reason is keeping regen working, not ageing.
clause_verbatim: Charging Limits. Adjust the charging limit (80%, 90%, 100%) via Controls > Energy section in the Ultraviolette App. Ultraviolette recommends setting a 90% charging limit to ensure that regenerative braking remains operational. [Printed p48. The stated reason for the limit is keeping regen available, not battery ageing.]

owner_action: Do not leave it parked at a high charge for long.
clause_verbatim: Avoid prolonged storage of the motorcycle at a high level of charge to avoid battery cell degradation. [Printed p47, under Battery Life.]

owner_action: Keep at least 50 to 60 percent past 30 days, wake it 30 minutes every 10 days, and use Deep Sleep past 10 days. Not doing so can affect cover.
clause_verbatim: Store indoors in a cool, dry location away from direct sunlight. Switch on the motorcycle for a minimum of 30 minutes every 10 days to charge the auxiliary battery. Activate Deep Sleep Mode if the motorcycle will not be used for more than 10 days. Maintain a minimum 50%-60% State of Charge (SoC) if storing for more than 30 days. Failure to follow these storage guidelines may affect the motorcycle's performance and warranty coverage. [Printed p74, under Storage Guidelines.]

owner_action: Do not leave the charger connected during long parking.
clause_verbatim: DO NOT leave the charger plugged in to the motorcycle during long term parking as it can affect charger and battery pack health. [Printed p74.]

owner_action: It will not charge above 50 degrees.
clause_verbatim: Charging does not occur if the temperature exceeds 50°C. [Printed p48.]

owner_action: Charge in a ventilated place, 20 metres clear of anything combustible.
clause_verbatim: Ensure to charge the motorcycle battery pack in a well-ventilated environment, at least 20 meters away from combustible substances. [Printed p47.]

owner_action: The storage rules are warranty-binding on the X-47 too.
clause_verbatim: Not following these storage instructions may affect motorcycle's performance and could void your warranty. [Printed p108, closing the Storage Guidelines, which carry the same 50 to 60 percent SoC rule as the F77 manual.]

owner_action: Charge to 100 percent at least once every 30 days.
clause_verbatim: Ensure that the battery is charged to 100% at least once in 30 days to maintain battery health. [Printed p3, under IMPORTANT THINGS TO KEEP IN MIND. Read from the rendered page by eye.]

owner_action: If it is standing, charge weekly or switch on vacation mode. Ola gives both a weekly and a 30 day interval on the same page.
clause_verbatim: If not using your scooter for long, keep charging it every week or activate the vacation mode to avoid complete discharge. [Printed p3. Note this sets a weekly interval while the bullet two lines below sets a 30 day one.]

owner_action: Do not keep riding it low. Ola says it affects battery health.
clause_verbatim: Extended or repeated driving at low battery level may impact battery health. If your battery level is low, charge as soon as possible. [Printed p3.]

owner_action: The socket and fittings must meet housing safety requirements, earthing included.
clause_verbatim: Ensure that the electric socket and fittings of the charging area are compliant with housing safety requirements including but not limited to proper earthing. [Printed p3.]

owner_action: Do not charge in a closed room.
clause_verbatim: Do not charge your scooter in closed confined spaces such as a closed room. [Printed p4, under DONT'S.]

owner_action: Tampering with wiring can void the warranty.
clause_verbatim: Don't tamper with components or electrical wirings as it may void your warranty. It might also cause a short-circuit, resulting in fire or electric shock. [Printed p4, under DONT'S.]

owner_action: Cover depends on storing, using and maintaining the bike as the manual says. The charging pages are part of that.
clause_verbatim: Ultraviolette warrants that motorcycles are free from defects in material and workmanship during the warranty coverage period, provided that the motorcycles are stored, used and maintained in accordance with the USER MANUAL. [Printed p95. This is the clause that pulls the manual's charging and storage sections into the warranty.]

owner_action: Do a full charge and a full discharge every six months or 72,000 km so the pack can re-reference itself. BYD will also test capacity for you.
clause_verbatim: To keep the power battery in optimal conditions, it should be fully charged and discharged regularly (once every 6 months or 72,000 km, whichever comes first) for self-calibration. A BYD authorized dealer or service provider may also be contacted to carry out capacity testing and calibration. [Printed p159, in a REMINDER box. BYD is the only maker in this dataset asking for a full discharge as well as a full charge, and the only one offering capacity testing.]

owner_action: Charging slows near the top because the pack is balancing cells. That is the system working, not a fault.
clause_verbatim: Battery balancing is enabled before charging is completed to improve service life. In such case, charging time may be prolonged. [Printed p82, under Charging Precautions. BYD runs LFP, and this is the same balancing mechanism JSW MG describes for the Windsor EV.]

owner_action: If it sits, charge it every three months, and fill it before a long lay-up.
clause_verbatim: If the vehicle is not expected to be driven for longer periods of time, make sure to fully charge its power battery before use. In case of idle periods, it is recommended to charge the battery every three months in order to prolong its service life. [Printed p82.]

owner_action: Arrive at a DC charger with a low charge and a warm pack. BYD says that is what makes it fast.
clause_verbatim: During DC charging, low temperatures and high SOC will reduce the charging current due to the battery's low temperature characteristics. Therefore, to improve charging speed, charging with a low SOC is recommended. To improve charging performance and user experience, charge the vehicle right after use, to take advantage of the battery's higher temperature. [Printed p82. BYD is the only maker here advising owners to arrive at a DC charger with a low state of charge and a warm pack.]

owner_action: Charge in a ventilated place with nobody sitting in the car.
clause_verbatim: The vehicle should be parked in a ventilated area, and there should not be any occupant inside when charging. [Printed p81, under Charging Precautions.]

owner_action: Use the chargers that came with the car at home, and only ARAI certified AC or DC chargers in public.
clause_verbatim: Always use the portable and wall-mount chargers supplied with the vehicle for private charging and ARAI certified AC or DC chargers for public charging. [Printed p20, closing the charger exclusion in Terms and Conditions - Standard Warranty. This is the only place in the dataset where a maker names a certification standard for public chargers.]
